changes.reason: Rename the ordering contract for atomic current-child readback. The local pre-submission Current check remains; each readback and recheck now proves authority and child contents at one cut instead of surrounding a child read with separate Current calls. The result and ordering assertions remain.

Rename the stale-authority contract around atomic current-child cuts. It still rejects stale authority before submission and at readback; a change after a completed cut must be rejected by the next recheck. All three boundaries retain refusal and event-order assertions.

Add the authenticated native-scope variant of the existing packet-boundary scenario. It needs CAP_BPF/CAP_NET_ADMIN and private network/bpffs namespaces, so ordinary cargo test ignores it. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest explicitly executes it; the original local-store case and shared scenario assertions remain.

Add authenticated native-scope coverage of coordinated GTP-U/DSCP opening. The new case requires privileged private kernel namespaces and is explicitly executed by the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The ordinary-test ignore does not remove the original local-store case or its shared assertions.

Add the native-scope adapter to the existing session ownership, undo, publication and backpressure scenario. Privileged private kernel namespaces require an ordinary-test ignore; the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest executes the new case and retains its local-store counterpart.

Add native-scope coverage of cancellation-safe shutdown and reset ownership. It requires privileged private kernel namespaces and runs explicitly in the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The original local-store case and the shared cancellation/drain assertions remain.

Add native-scope authority to the existing XFRM expiration/acquire/undo scenario. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest explicitly runs this privileged private-namespace case; it is ignored only by ordinary cargo test. The original local-store case and shared assertions remain.

Add native-scope coverage that rebuilding an authority adapter cannot reinstall a retired effect. Privileged private-namespace execution is owned by the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The original local-store test and the shared consumption/reinstall assertions remain.

Add native-scope coverage to the existing XFRM partial-effect, panic, cancellation and lost-publication-reply scenario. This new privileged private-namespace case is explicitly run by the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. Its local-store counterpart and shared assertions remain.

Add the authenticated native-scope variant of the real-quorum XFRM publication/store-loss scenario. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest runs it with its necessary kernel privileges and private namespaces. The original local-store case and its scenario assertions remain.

Add native-scope coverage of unknown committed replies and stale-child refusal. The case requires kernel privileges/private namespaces and is explicitly included in the required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest. The original local-store test and its shared refusal assertions remain.

Add native-scope authority to the existing opening, interrupted containment removal and publication scenario, including native work-class checks. The required local-kernel-lifecycle manifest runs this privileged private-namespace case. The original local-store case and its shared assertions remain.

Denied operational events now omit per-event audit work. The former audit-record assertions are replaced by an empty audit sink assertion; authenticated hidden-event and blocked-audit regressions cover omission and independent authorization termination.

Subtree scalar content matching is now supported under RFC 6241 section 6.2.5. The replacement checks bounded tree retention without flattening; authenticated generated-service tests cover matching, authorization, masking and resource limits.

Split the ordinary i686 lane by Cargo test binary to avoid its 30-minute job timeout. The ordinary slice retains the library and its existing ten exact exclusions, which still run in contracts. The ordinary-integration slice runs every registered integration target via --test *, all session-net doctests, and the unchanged opc-protocol/opc-proto-gtpv2c command. Both ordinary slices and contracts remain required by the same i686 aggregate. The named inventory partitions exactly as 807 + 572 = 1379, with no missing, extra or duplicate tests; all three doctest targets, features, profiles and test-thread limits are retained.

Rename the snapshot-origin purge regression to describe physical prefix reclamation. The test now requires covered rows to be absent through export and cold catalog reopen, while preserving its payload, membership, snapshot, and lineage assertions.

Transfer misc library execution to the required rust-libraries matrix using the explicit --split-libraries precheck/plan mode. The logical coverage plan still owns every original command; live compiled-library inventories partition exact names across two required runners with identical workspace packages, features, profiles, ignored status and test-thread counts. Scope-payload and child-read contracts remain fresh serial processes before ordinary execution on library shard 0. Binary unit tests, examples, doctests and the heavy remainder stay on misc. The three full-bound proofs move to dedicated required native-log shards with unchanged O1 commands, input sizes and assertions. Planner regressions cover total/disjoint identity ownership, future siblings, wrong-profile and overlap mutations, real Cargo execution including test=false libraries, and missing workflow dependencies. Existing job budgets and all test deadlines are unchanged.

Pre-Vote and precise election evaluation prevent the stale survivor from consuming the next term. Replace the obsolete expected authority timeout with recovery through the unchanged 26-second helper. The replacement preserves divergent 12/13 log prefixes and checks both real Pre-Vote replies, the fresh survivor's one persisted vote, fresh local authority, and reconciliation of both survivors.

The precise election timer now recovers from the retained real split vote before the unchanged 26-second transition bound. Replace the obsolete leaderless-at-deadline checkpoint with actual split-term checks and recovery before the same bound. Normal-time setup can also collapse 100 ms ticker phases: replace the distinct-phase setup assertions with observed aligned tick registrations and distinct finite RNG samples that order two genuine inquiries, crossed persisted votes, and one automatic retry. The history, retention, snapshot, reconciliation and durable-vote assertions remain. Local-helper assertion count changes from 163 to 160.
